record.original_question: Suppose one studies parking on trees or connected components formed by parked cars when either the offspring distribution of the underlying random tree or the distributions of car arrivals have infinite third moment and tail behavior of the form c * k^{-gamma} for some constant c and gamma in (3, 4). Whether one looks at strongly connected or weakly connected components, is the critical component size of order n^{(gamma-2)/(gamma-1)}?

evidence.quote: In the above paper, Contat conjectures that no matter if one considers strongly or weakly connected components, when the offspring distribution of the tree or the car arrivals distributions have an infinite third moments and a tail of order c • k^{-gamma} for some constant c and some gamma in (3, 4) when k goes to infinity, the size of the components should be of order n^{(gamma-2)/(gamma-1)} at criticality.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the parking process on a random rooted tree defined as follows. Let $T_n$ be a rooted tree with $n$ vertices (for instance, a Bienaymé–Galton–Watson tree conditioned to have $n$ vertices, with a given offspring distribution $\mu$ on $\{0,1,2,\dots\}$ of mean $1$). Independently, on each vertex $v$ of $T_n$ place a random number $A_v$ of cars, where the $(A_v)$ are i.i.d. with distribution $\nu$ on $\{0,1,2,\dots\}$. Each car tries to park on its starting vertex; if that vertex is occupied, the car drives toward the root and parks at the first empty vertex it encounters, leaving the tree if it reaches the root while every vertex on its path is occupied. The system is at criticality in a suitable sense (e.g., the mean number of cars per vertex is tuned so that the proportion of cars exiting the tree undergoes a phase transition).

Define a strongly connected component as a maximal subtree of vertices that are all occupied by parked cars, and a weakly connected component (a "cluster") as a maximal connected set of vertices that have been visited by at least one car during the parking procedure.

Assume that at least one of the distributions $\mu$ or $\nu$ has infinite third moment with a power-law tail of the form
$$\mu(k) \sim c\, k^{-\gamma} \quad \text{or} \quad \nu(k) \sim c\, k^{-\gamma} \qquad \text{as } k \to \infty,$$
for some constant $c>0$ and some exponent $\gamma \in (3,4)$.

Prove or disprove: at criticality, the size of the largest strongly connected component, and equally the size of the largest weakly connected component, is of order
$$n^{(\gamma-2)/(\gamma-1)}.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The statement is described as a conjecture due to Contat regarding heavy-tailed parking processes on random trees. Web searches return the survey listing it as an open conjecture and related works (parking on Cayley trees, supercritical geometric BGW trees, parking with given degree sequence) that establish neighboring results but do not prove this heavy-tail critical scaling. No published proof of the n^{(γ-2)/(γ-1)} scaling at criticality was found.

status_evidence.title: Short survey of results and open problems for parking problems on random trees
status_evidence.snippet: Contat conjectures that no matter if one considers strongly or weakly connected components, when the offspring distribution of the tree or the car arrivals distributions have an infinite third moments and a tail of order c·k^{-γ} ... the size of the components should be of order n^{(γ-2)/(γ-1)} at criticality.
status_evidence.claim: Stated as an open conjecture in a recent survey of parking problems on random trees.

status_evidence.title: Parking on supercritical geometric Bienaymé–Galton–Watson trees
status_evidence.snippet: Provides a criterion for the phase of the parking process but does not establish the heavy-tail critical scaling exponent.
status_evidence.claim: Related work that does not resolve the heavy-tailed critical exponent conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Parking on trees with a (random) given degree sequence and the Frozen configuration model
status_evidence.snippet: Studies parking with given degree sequences; addresses related but not identical scaling questions.
status_evidence.claim: Related results on parking and degree sequences without resolving the conjecture.
